en.display_text:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with reference to the status of women in Vedic society?

(a) Swayamvara practice — became increasingly standardized and widespread as a marriage institution in the Later Vedic period, reflecting women's retained agency
(b) Maitreyi — evidence of mainstream Upanayana access for women in the Later Vedic period due to her documented philosophical knowledge
(c) Rigvedic brahmavadini tradition — represents a contrast to the Later Vedic period, when women were progressively excluded from Upanayana and formal Vedic learning
(d) Child marriage — firmly established as a universally codified Later Vedic norm in Brahmana texts, with no further development needed in subsequent Dharmashastra literature
en.strong_distractor: b — Students who know Maitreyi is associated with philosophical discussions may assume she performed Upanayana — conflating philosophical engagement with formal ritual initiation.
elimination_logic: Option a incorrectly attributes Swayamvara as an expanding institution — it was declining in the Later Vedic period; eliminate a.
Option b attributes Upanayana to Maitreyi in the Later Vedic period — Maitreyi is an Upanishadic transitional figure but not evidence of mainstream Upanayana for women; eliminate b.

Option c correctly pairs the Rigvedic brahmavadini tradition (women scholars who composed hymns, like Lopamudra) with their contrast to the Later Vedic norm of women's exclusion from Upanayana; select c.
Option d incorrectly describes child marriage as an established Later Vedic norm — it has roots in the period but became fully established in post-Vedic Dharmashastra texts; eliminate d.
en.upsc_trap_explanation: The Maitreyi trap in option b exploits the association between Maitreyi and philosophical knowledge. Students who know Maitreyi discussed Atman and Brahman with Yajnavalkya may infer she had formal Upanayana — but philosophical discussion in an Upanishadic context is not the same as formal ritual initiation. Maitreyi is exceptional precisely as a transitional figure; mainstream Later Vedic women did not have Upanayana access.
en.final_explanation:
The status of women's education and ritual rights in the Later Vedic period is marked by a clear decline from the Rigvedic period.

• Option (a): Incorrectly matched — Swayamvara was declining, not expanding, in the Later Vedic period. The direction is wrong.
• Option (b): Incorrectly matched — Maitreyi is a philosophical figure from the Upanishadic transitional period who engaged in discussions with Yajnavalkya. This does not constitute evidence of mainstream Upanayana for women; her exceptional status as a brahmavadini does not represent the norm.
• Option (c): Correctly matched — The Rigvedic brahmavadini tradition (represented by Lopamudra, Vishwavara, Apala — women who composed Rigvedic hymns) stands in clear contrast to the Later Vedic exclusion of women from Upanayana and formal Vedic learning. This correctly paired contrast is the answer.
• Option (d): Incorrectly matched — Child marriage has roots in the Later Vedic period but became an 'established norm' codified in post-Vedic Dharmashastra texts; characterizing it as a firmly established Later Vedic institution overstates the evidence.

Value Addition:
• Lopamudra is credited with composing Rigveda 1.179 (dialogue with her husband Agastya) — a brahmavadini example.
• Vishwavara and Apala are other Rigvedic women scholars (brahmavadinis) who composed hymns.
• The Grihyasutras — early post-Vedic domestic ritual texts — contain explicit restrictions on women's Upanayana, marking the formal codification of the exclusion.

उत्तर वैदिक काल में महिलाओं की शिक्षा और संस्कार अधिकारों की स्थिति ऋग्वैदिक काल की तुलना में स्पष्ट रूप से गिरावट दर्शाती है।

• विकल्प (a): गलत मेल — स्वयंवर उत्तर वैदिक काल में घट रहा था, बढ़ रहा नहीं था। दिशा गलत है।
• विकल्प (b): गलत मेल — मैत्रेयी उपनिषदकालीन संक्रमणकालीन दार्शनिक व्यक्तित्व हैं जिन्होंने याज्ञवल्क्य के साथ संवाद किया। यह महिलाओं के लिए मुख्यधारा उपनयन का प्रमाण नहीं है; उनका असाधारण ब्रह्मवादिनी होना सामान्य स्थिति का प्रतिनिधित्व नहीं करता।
• विकल्प (c): सही मेल — ऋग्वैदिक ब्रह्मवादिनी परंपरा (लोमपद्रा, विश्ववरा, अपाला जैसे ऋग्वेद की स्त्री विदुषकाएँ) स्पष्ट रूप से उत्तर वैदिक काल में महिलाओं के उपनयन और औपचारिक वैदिक शिक्षा से बहिष्कार के विपरीत है। यह सही जोड़ी गई तुलना उत्तर है।
• विकल्प (d): गलत मेल — बाल विवाह की जड़ें उत्तर वैदिक काल में हैं लेकिन यह पश्च वैदिक धर्मशास्त्र ग्रंथों में 'स्थापित नियम' के रूप में विकसित हुआ; इसे उत्तर वैदिक काल की पूरी तरह स्थापित संस्था कहना अतिशयोक्ति है।

Value Addition:
• लोमपद्रा को ऋग्वेद 1.179 (अपने पति अगस्त्य के साथ संवाद) की रचना का श्रेय दिया जाता है — एक ब्रह्मवादिनी उदाहरण।
• विश्ववरा और अपाला अन्य ऋग्वैदिक स्त्री विदुषकाएँ (ब्राह्मवादिनी) हैं जिन्होंने मंत्र रचे।
• गृह्यसूत्र — प्रारंभिक पश्च वैदिक घरेलू संस्कार ग्रंथ — महिलाओं के उपनयन पर स्पष्ट प्रतिबंध रखते हैं, जो बहिष्कार का औपचारिक संहिताकरण है।
